notes:
Status: CLOSED-LOST (churn to hyperscaler managed endpoints)

Summary:
- Prospect: Ironwood Inference Labs (platform provider for enterprise search + support workflows). Evaluated Redwood Private and Dedicated for low-latency reranking + semantic search.
- Outcome: Procurement signed with hyperscaler (AWS SageMaker real-time endpoints) in Jan 2026. Primary reasons: existing enterprise AWS commit, procurement preference for native managed services, and quicker path to enterprise-approved IAM + billing integration.

Timeline (bulleted):
- 2025-10-15: Lead created; initial qualification with Maya Chen. Use-case: semantic search for 40M doc corpus, reranking for clickthrough optimization.
- 2025-11-02: Intro demo (Maya + Elliot SE). POC agreed: 6-week pilot for embeddings + reranking. Fireflies: ff_20260114_ironwood_intro.
- 2025-12-08: POC kickoff; dataset ingestion and baseline Redwood hosted run. SE notes: cache hit-rate favorable, latency within SLA on Dedicated estimate.
- 2026-01-14: POC review — quality OK, cost estimate competitive vs in-house. Security raised HSM/KMS integration and export controls (legal). Fireflies: ff_20260127_poc-review.
- 2026-01-20: Procurement asks for 3-way comparison including AWS managed endpoints. AWS demonstrated simpler operational model and direct discount under enterprise agreement.
- 2026-01-30: Budget review — finance flagged committed cloud credits with AWS, recommended native endpoints to centralize spend. Last activity recorded.
- 2026-02-04: Final security gating: internal security favored AWS native because of in-house IAM, existing VPC endpoints, and audited KMS flows.
- 2026-02-10: Contract decision: chose AWS SageMaker real-time endpoints. Opportunity closed-lost.

Key win/loss factors (notes):
- Lost to hyperscaler because of procurement rules and existing cloud credits; not strictly technical.
- Technical: Redwood hit quality and latency targets in POC. The sticking points were (a) HSM/KMS workflow required by infosec — they wanted single-pane KMS under their AWS tenancy, (b) preference for managed autoscaling and billing on the same cloud account, (c) internal ops head declined additional vendor onboarding.
- Business: Estimated ARR fit, but finance prioritized consolidated cloud spend; signing with hyperscaler gave them immediate cost predictability via committed discounts.
- People/process: No senior engineering champion to fight for third-party vendor; champion (eng manager) rotated roles mid-POC.
